newsitem.title: TAIWAN: U.S. to help Taiwan, China join WTO - paper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to help Taiwan, China join WTO - paper.

text.p: The United States has promised to help rivals China and Taiwan join the World Trade Organisation before July 1, 1997, Taiwan's mass circulation United Daily News reported on Thursday.
The newspaper, quoting unidentified sources, said Taiwan's Presidential Office and related government agencies had been informed about Washington's pledge.
Taiwan would speed up bilateral and multilateral negotiations with other WTO members, including the United States, the newspaper said.
Taiwan officials declined to comment on the report.
Economics Minister Wang Chih-kang said the government realised that it would be difficult for Taiwan to join the world trade body if Beijing became a member before Taipei, the newspaper said.

The U.S. decision to help Beijing in its WTO bid before 1997 was aimed at preventing China from taking advantage of Hong Kong's existing WTO membership without fulfilling its obligations after 1997, it said.
Taiwan has urged the world trade body not to be swayed by China's political agenda when considering its entry.
China has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war separated them in 1949. It has said the island is not entitled to join any international organisation.
Taiwan applied in 1990 to join WTO's predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, under the name of Chinese Taipei.
China's application to join GATT by the end of 1994 was rejected.
GATT was replaced by WTO in January 1995.
